I’d avoid a plain “accepted, please come and pick them up.” With 80 older laptops, some cracked/damaged, you should accept **only conditionally**, with proof of compliant handling and data sanitisation. That way you keep the “win-win” while protecting your firm from data leaks, e-waste liability, or customs/export problems.

Here is a professional reply you can send.

---

**Subject:** Pickup of legacy laptops – acceptance subject to compliance and data security requirements

Dear [Name],

Thank you for your offer to take our 80 legacy laptops. We are open to proceeding, subject to the following conditions:

1. **Compliance with Swiss export and Ghana import/e-waste rules**  
   Please confirm that your business is legally authorised to import and process the equipment in Ghana. If any of the devices are considered waste or mixed waste/equipment, please provide the required permits, prior informed consent, or other regulatory documentation. We cannot ship the devices unless the transfer is compliant.

2. **Reuse or certified recycling only**  
   The laptops must either be genuinely reused/refurbished or sent to a certified recycler. Please confirm in writing that you will not leave any unit in informal or unregulated disposal channels. For devices that cannot be reused, we will require an end-of-life or certified recycling certificate.

3. **Data protection and secure wiping**  
   All laptops will be sanitised/securely erased before handover, in line with our internal data protection procedures. If any device cannot be securely erased or verified, we will require the storage media to be physically destroyed or returned to us for certified destruction. Please provide a data destruction certificate for any storage media that you handle.

4. **Asset documentation**  
   Before pickup, we will provide an asset list including model, serial number, condition notes, and confirmation of data sanitisation. We ask that you sign a collection/handover note at pickup.

5. **Final report**  
   Within [14] days after pickup, please provide a final report including photos, reuse/refurbishment or recycling certificates, and confirmation of customs clearance/import documentation.

6. **Logistics and responsibility**  
   You will be responsible for pickup, packing, export documentation, transport, insurance, and any import duties or fees unless otherwise agreed in writing. Risk and responsibility will pass to you once the signed handover note is completed.

If you are able to confirm the above, please let us know a suitable pickup date and location. If you cannot provide the required documentation or proof of compliant processing, we will need to use our certified recycler instead.

Kind regards,  
[Your Name]  
[Your Position]  
[Company Name]

---

A slightly shorter version, if you want to keep it friendly but still safe:

> Dear [Name],  
>   
> Thank you for the offer. We would be happy to proceed with you collecting the 80 laptops, provided that:  
>   
> 1. all devices are securely wiped before handover;  
> 2. the transfer complies with Swiss export, waste/e-waste, and Ghana import requirements;  
> 3. any non-reusable devices are sent to a certified recycler, not informal disposal; and  
> 4. you provide a signed handover note plus a final certificate/report showing how the devices were reused or recycled.  
>   
> If you can confirm this in writing, please let us know a suitable pickup date.  
>   
> Best regards,  
> [Your Name]

---

Before pickup, I would also have your team do these quick checks:

- **Wipe all drives**: Do not trust old operating systems or passwords. Use proper disk wiping / secure erase. If a laptop will not boot, consider physically destroying the SSD/HDD or returning it to your recycler unless you are sure it is safe.
- **Remove personal labels**: Names, email addresses, employee IDs, stickers, etc.
- **Take photos**: Each laptop, serial number, screen condition, and any damage.
- **Keep a serial-number register**: Useful if any device later turns up as e-waste or causes a compliance issue.
- **Check batteries**: If any battery is swollen, leaking, or damaged, do not include it in a normal shipment; use specialist handling.
- **Do not misdeclare**: If the devices are being sent for reuse, declare them accurately. If they are waste, do not label them as “gifts” or “new equipment” just to make customs easier.
- **Get written confirmation from the trader**: A one-line email saying “I confirm the devices will be imported and processed legally in Ghana and will not be disposed of informally” is better than nothing.

Red flags: if the trader is vague about recycling, refuses to give certificates, wants everything shipped quickly without paperwork, or says “we’ll sort out the permits later,” I would not hand over the batch. In that case, the certified recycler is the safer option even if it costs more.
